evals.name: existing-module-adoption
evals.prompt: Audit a legacy JVM reactor. Module A has high coverage, module B has low coverage, an aggregate report looks healthy, and the team asks for a universal coverage target. No policy changes have been authorized.
expectations: Reports module-specific evidence instead of treating the aggregate as adequate enforcement.
Measures existing floors and proposes reviewed adoption decisions without inventing a universal percentage.
Does not change thresholds or broaden generated-code exclusions during the audit.
Distinguishes audit authority from setup authorization.

evals.name: missing-data-and-empty-modules
evals.prompt: Our verify job is green when coverage agents are removed. We also have a POM aggregator, a test-only module, and a production module with no tests. Fix the quality gap.
expectations: Requires fresh expected execution data and expected production classes/counters, not just successful report/check goals.
Checks the incremental path after a prior successful run to rule out stale coverage.
Handles aggregator and test-only modules deliberately without exempting untested production code.
Includes a deliberate missing-instrumentation failure and verifies the diagnostic.

evals.name: ordinary-development-no-upgrade
evals.prompt: Add tests for this JVM bug. The repo has pinned tooling and a working canonical CI command. You notice newer formatter and analyzer releases are available.
expectations: Uses project pins and existing canonical verification.
Does not upgrade unrelated tools or reformat untouched code.
Adds meaningful tests for changed behavior.
Does not weaken floors, exclusions or findings to pass.

evals.name: setup-version-and-vulnerability-policy
evals.prompt: Set up quality policy for a new mixed JVM project. Give reusable guidance for selecting tool versions, runtime compatibility, dependency scanning and CI.
expectations: Distinguishes tool JDK, runtime, bytecode and API target.
Resolves stable compatible releases from official sources at setup and pins them in the project.
Keeps reusable skill guidance free of specific tool release pins and distinguishes adapter/engine versions.
Defines scanning cadence, severity/failure and reviewed expiring exceptions as explicit project decisions.
Names a required CI path for all gates and separates compatibility jobs where needed.
